beats.text: He did not give himself an ulcer.
beats.note: Discover says he developed gastritis, the precursor to an ulcer. The Lasker Foundation says he did not develop an ulcer.
Scientific American describes the prevailing theory as a psychosomatic illness caused by too much stress. The Lasker Foundation adds excess stomach acid.
The Lasker Foundation reports the bacterium did not grow in animal stomachs, so there was no animal model to prove it.

beats.text: In July 1984 he drank the broth himself.
beats.note: Discover says he took H. pylori from a patient, stirred it into a broth and drank it. Scientific American says he asked neither an ethics commission nor his wife.
The Lasker Foundation reports the endoscopy, then a course of antibiotics to clear the infection.

beats.context: In the 1982 study of 100 patients, 77 per cent of those with stomach ulcers carried H. pylori. The Lasker Foundation reports it.

beats.name: Barry Marshall and Robin Warren
beats.role: Shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the bacterium Helicobacter pylori and its role in gastritis and peptic ulcer disease.

beats.text: He drank the evidence, then took the antibiotics.

beats.line: Sometimes the proof is in the glass.
